formulation.rationale: This split child contains only the fixed 70/30 insulin aspart protamine/insulin aspart premix. The parent group was split because rapid-acting aspart products and this premix require different fasting-management logic.

comparisons.note: The Austrian Diabetes Association position statement directly addresses patients using mixed insulin for routine operations and recommends conversion to long-acting insulin at approximately two-thirds of the original mixed-insulin standard dose.

comparisons.checked_locators: Management of insulin; perioperative insulin discussion
comparisons.note: The Brazilian anesthesiology society review directly addresses premixed insulin, including the day before surgery and day-of-surgery separation into intermediate and fast components.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: The current US colonoscopy consensus explicitly states that antihyperglycemic management should be individualized with the prescribing clinician and is beyond this bowel-preparation document's scope; it gives no premixed-insulin dose instruction.

recommendations.timing_text: It is not necessary to change the dose on the day before surgery.
recommendations.applicability: General perioperative management of a patient using premixed insulin when the fasting period is limited.
recommendations.exceptions: This is perioperative surgery guidance rather than a colonoscopy-specific premix protocol; the USMSTF states that antihyperglycemic management around colonoscopy should be individualized.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian anesthesiology society review states that premixed-insulin dose change is not necessary on the day before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: auf ein langwirksames Insulin (1 oder 2 × täglich gespritzt) umgestellt werden
recommendations.applicability: Patient using conventional mixed-insulin therapy for a routine operation.
recommendations.exceptions: The position statement is general perioperative guidance and does not specifically name colonoscopy. USMSTF requires individualized prescriber-assisted antihyperglycemic management for colonoscopy.
recommendations.summary: The Austrian Diabetes Association recommends switching mixed insulin to long-acting insulin for routine operations.

recommendations.qualifier: dose after switch to long-acting insulin
recommendations.timing_text: etwa zwei Drittel der Standarddosis des ursprünglichen Mischinsulins
recommendations.applicability: Dose of the long-acting insulin used after conversion from mixed insulin for a routine operation.
recommendations.exceptions: This is a source-quoted proportional framework, not a patient-specific calculated dose.
recommendations.summary: The Austrian position statement describes the long-acting replacement dose as approximately two-thirds of the original mixed-insulin standard dose.

recommendations.timing_text: on the day of surgery, they should be replaced by those of intermediate and fast action
recommendations.applicability: Patient using premixed insulin on the day of surgery.
recommendations.exceptions: The source advises administering the intermediate and fast components independently to reduce fasting hypoglycemia risk from the fast-acting component.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian anesthesiology society review recommends replacing premixed insulin with separate intermediate- and fast-acting components on the day of surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: proportionally reduce the morning dose by 25–50%
recommendations.applicability: Morning intermediate-acting component after the premixed preparation has been separated for the day of surgery.
recommendations.exceptions: The recommendation applies to the intermediate-acting component after separation; it is not a 25–50% reduction of the entire fixed premix.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian review recommends reducing the morning intermediate-acting component by 25–50%.

scenario_coverage.reason: The Brazilian anesthesiology society review explicitly addresses the day before surgery for premixed insulin.
The Austrian Diabetes Association and Brazilian anesthesiology society sources both address mixed/premixed insulin on the day of a routine operation, but recommend different conversion strategies.

The compared primary society sources did not provide a sufficiently specific post-procedure instruction for restarting this fixed 70/30 premix, and USMSTF leaves antihyperglycemic medication management around colonoscopy to individualized prescribing-clinician guidance.

conflicts.description: The Austrian Diabetes Association recommends converting mixed insulin to long-acting insulin at approximately two-thirds of the original mixed-insulin standard dose for routine operations, whereas the Brazilian anesthesiology society review recommends replacing premixed insulin with separately administered intermediate- and fast-acting components and reducing the intermediate morning component by 25–50%. These strategies are preserved separately and not averaged.

open_questions.text: For colonoscopy specifically, the USMSTF states that antihyperglycemic management should be individualized with the prescribing clinician; the clinician reviewer should determine which perioperative premix strategy is appropriate for local practice and the patient's fasting schedule.
No compared primary society source supplied a sufficiently specific post-procedure restart instruction for the fixed NovoLog Mix 70/30 product, so no restart dose or timing was inferred.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package. The fixed premix was split from rapid-acting insulin aspart products before research. Day-of-procedure society recommendations conflict and are intentionally preserved without synthesis into a single unsupported regimen.
